1.explanation:
1. DataTable.js: this file defines the render prop API and the prop getters (getTableContainerProps and getTableProps). Currently getTableContainerProps does not generate or return any IDs for the title/description nodes, and getTableProps does not inject aria-labelledby/aria-describedby into the . 2. TableContainer.js: this file renders the

(title) and

(description) but does not accept or generate IDs on those elements, so there’s no way to reference them externally. It needs to be updated to accept a base id (from getTableContainerProps) and assign derived IDs to the title and description, e.g. “${baseId}__title” and “${baseId}__description”. By updating these two files, the DataTable component can automatically wire up the correct ARIA references for consumers, and screen readers will announce the table’s visible title/description instead of the cell contents.
1.bug_scenario:
The DataTable’s TableContainer renders a visible title and description but does not assign any IDs to those elements. As a result, consumers cannot hook up aria-labelledby or aria-describedby on the <Table> to point at the title/description nodes. Without proper IDs exposed, screen readers like JAWS fall back to reading the table’s cell contents as the label (concatenating the first few cells).

The screenshots show a user giving TableContainer an arbitrary id ("table_container") and manually adding aria-labelledby="table_container" to the <Table>, but since TableContainer doesn’t render an element with that id, the browser ignores the reference. Likewise there’s no id on the description, so aria-describedby cannot be applied to the Table.

To fix this, TableContainer must generate unique IDs for its title and description elements (e.g. "xx__title" and "xx__description"), and DataTable’s getTableProps must include both aria-labelledby and aria-describedby pointing to those IDs so authors don’t have to wire it up themselves.
